title: The gases and compounds that can be in an atmosphere: identity, phase points, heat capacity, Rayleigh scattering, Henry constants, viscosity, infrared bands, ultraviolet and visible absorption (GEN.410)
sources: chemicals 1.5.2 (heos_constants, critical, triple and vapour-pressure tables), thermo 0.6.1, periodictable 2.1.0, cantera nasa_gas.yaml, NIST WebBook and NIST fluid saturation tables, Yaws and CRC values as tagged in part 01
He et al. 2021, ACP 21, 14927 (N2O, CH4, CO2, O2 refractivity); [R3470]; Mansfield and Peck; Bideau-Mehu et al.; Cuthbertson; Allen/Cox; NIST CCCBDB polarizabilities as read in part 02
[R4066] gas-phase fundamentals at [R0620] as read in part 03 table 2.1; photochem_clima_data 0.3.4 ([R1873, R2040, R2258, R3966], [R2302, R2303]) binned to 35 bins in part 02 section 2.3
notes: Each block of a row has its own status word from the research part (DATA, COMPUTED, READ, 2ND-HAND, NOT REACHED); `state` and `limit` are the row's source state in the vocabulary of GEN.472. The molar mass in the file is the research part's, kept for the audit; the loader computes the working value from `physics.elements` (GEN.438). Rayleigh sigma is per molecule in cm2; `reference_temperature_k` is the temperature the refractivity fit was made at (GEN.408). Henry constants are mol/(kg bar) at 298.15 K with d = -dln kH/d(1/T) in K; viscosity needs the Lennard-Jones sigma (Angstrom) and epsilon/k (K). `infrared` lists the band centres (cm-1) the research gives, `approximate` where it writes 'about'; `uv` holds each gas's mean photoabsorption cross section (cm2 per molecule) in the bins of `uv_bins_nm`, `null` outside the data and `partial_bin` where under half of the bin is covered.

rayleigh.research_note: report gives n - 1 = 2.362e-4 at 550 nm with unknown reference temperature: n-based sigma is 3.11e-27 (if 288.15 K) or 2.80e-27 (if 273.15 K); the generic formula with alpha = 1.501 A^3 gives 3.38e-27, 9 to 21 percent above. Use the report value
